Vulnerabilities.Title: It was found that apt-key in apt, all versions, do not correctly valid ...
Vulnerabilities.Description: It was found that apt-key in apt, all versions, do not correctly validate gpg keys with the master keyring, leading to a potential man-in-the-middle attack.

Vulnerabilities.Title: [Privilege escalation possible to other user than root]
util-linux: util-linux: failed external mount helper still runs privileged X-mount post-hooks
Vulnerabilities.Description: util-linux versions through 2.41.5 and 2.42.2 fail to check mount helper exit status before running post-mount hooks, allowing unprivileged users to execute privileged operations on pre-existing filesystems. Attackers can exploit X-mount.idmap or X-mount.owner hooks to clone filesystems with inherited suid bits or modify target inode permissions after a helper fails, achieving privilege escalation.

Vulnerabilities.Title: util-linux: util-linux: nsenter --join-cgroup leaks root cgroup migration authority
Vulnerabilities.Description: The nsenter --join-cgroup option opens the target cgroup.procs file as root and leaves that file descriptor open across later namespace and credential changes and across execve(). Because the kernel checks later cgroup migrations using the credentials from the original open, a program run in an attacker-controlled target can inherit root's ability to move host processes between cgroups. After a privileged operator uses --join-cgroup against that target, an unprivileged user can migrate and terminate unrelated root processes.

Vulnerabilities.Title: util-linux: util-linux: X-mount.subdir detached-tree resolution can escape via intermediate symlinks
Vulnerabilities.Description: The X-mount.subdir option uses a detached-tree fast path on Linux 6.15 and later and passes the configured subdirectory to open_tree() with AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW. That flag does not stop intermediate symlink traversal or keep resolution inside the newly mounted filesystem. A local unprivileged user with an fstab-authorized X-mount.subdir entry can attach a host path at the intended mountpoint.

Vulnerabilities.Title: util-linux: util-linux: restricted bind mounts do not pin the source, allowing X-mount.owner/group/mode redirection
Vulnerabilities.Description: A flaw was found in util-linux. Restricted bind mounts take the source path from fstab but do not pin that source before the privileged mount. A local unprivileged user who can replace the authorized source or a writable ancestor can redirect SUID mount(8) to bind another host directory. If the fstab entry also sets X-mount.owner, X-mount.group, or X-mount.mode, root then changes ownership or mode on that redirected inode.

Vulnerabilities.Title: util-linux: util-linux: Access control bypass due to improper hostname canonicalization
Vulnerabilities.Description: A flaw was found in util-linux. Improper hostname canonicalization in the `login(1)` utility, when invoked with the `-h` option, can modify the supplied remote hostname before setting `PAM_RHOST`. A remote attacker could exploit this by providing a specially crafted hostname, potentially bypassing host-based Pluggable Authentication Modules (PAM) access control rules that rely on fully qualified domain names. This could lead to unauthorized access.

Vulnerabilities.Title: util-linux: partial disclosure of arbitrary files in chfn and chsh when compiled with libreadline
Vulnerabilities.Description: A flaw was found in the util-linux chfn and chsh utilities when compiled with Readline support. The Readline library uses an "INPUTRC" environment variable to get a path to the library config file. When the library cannot parse the specified file, it prints an error message containing data from the file. This flaw allows an unprivileged user to read root-owned files, potentially leading to privilege escalation. This flaw affects util-linux versions prior to 2.37.4.

Vulnerabilities.Title: coreutils: race condition vulnerability in chown and chgrp
Vulnerabilities.Description: In GNU Coreutils through 8.29, chown-core.c in chown and chgrp does not prevent replacement of a plain file with a symlink during use of the POSIX "-R -L" options, which allows local users to modify the ownership of arbitrary files by leveraging a race condition.

Vulnerabilities.Title: coreutils: Heap Buffer Under-Read in GNU Coreutils sort via Key Specification
Vulnerabilities.Description: A flaw was found in GNU Coreutils. The sort utility's begfield() function is vulnerable to a heap buffer under-read. The program may access memory outside the allocated buffer if a user runs a crafted command using the traditional key format. A malicious input could lead to a crash or leak sensitive data.

Vulnerabilities.Title: coreutils: GNU coreutils uniq: Denial of Service and information disclosure via out-of-bounds read with multibyte input
Vulnerabilities.Description:
GNU coreutils uniq is vulnerable to an out‑of‑bounds read due to incorrect handling of multibyte input when the -w (--check-chars) option is used. The find_field() function miscalculates the byte length of characters by repeatedly processing a fixed pointer instead of advancing through the input, resulting in an inflated length value. 
This incorrect length is later used in a memcmp operation, causing reads beyond the allocated buffer when processing crafted multibyte input.

When running GNU coreutils uniq with attacker-provided arguments, this behavior leads to a crash and potential adjacent heap memory exposure.


This issue has been fixed in the commit d64e35a8a4c0e4608321433e0d84d917e4e36371.

Vulnerabilities.Title: coreutils: GNU coreutils unexpand: Denial of Service via crafted tab stop values
Vulnerabilities.Description:
GNU coreutils unexpand is vulnerable to a heap-based buffer overflow due to an integer overflow during buffer allocation when processing large tab stop (-t) values. The multiplication used to calculate the allocation size can wrap around, resulting in an undersized buffer.
When processing crafted input, subsequent writes exceed the allocated memory, leading to an out‑of‑bounds heap write.

When running GNU coreutils unexpand with attacker-provided large tab stop (-t) arguments, this behavior leads to a crash and potentially achieve a heap write primitive depending on memory layout.










This issue has been fixed in the commit b60a159fdc5bfcf9988d3a4cb6f53abe8ad5d35d

Vulnerabilities.Title: dash: dash: Super-polynomial backtracking in pmatch when libc fnmatch is disabled
Vulnerabilities.Description: A flaw was found in dash. When built without libc fnmatch, the internal pmatch() matcher implements * by unbounded recursion over candidate positions. A local user who can plant filenames, or otherwise feed that matcher, can make a short multi-star pattern such as *.*.*.*.*.tar.gz consume excessive CPU.

Vulnerabilities.Title: dash: dash: Heap out-of-bounds write in conv_escape via undersized Unicode escape reservation
Vulnerabilities.Description: A flaw was found in dash. The printf builtin reserves four bytes before converting a Unicode \u or \U escape, but the multi-byte token can need five or six bytes. A local user who can supply such an escape to dash printf or echo %b, including through dash -c and a positional argument, can write one or two bytes past that reservation.

Vulnerabilities.Title: diffutils: heap‑based buffer overflow due to multiple signed integer overflows in line‑mapping calculations
Vulnerabilities.Description:
diff3 tool from GNU diffutils is vulnerable to a heap‑based buffer overflow due to multiple signed integer overflows in line‑mapping calculations. Incorrect arithmetic in mapping line ranges can result in corrupted values being used for memory allocation and loop bounds.
When processing crafted diff output, these overflows may cause the application to allocate insufficient memory and subsequently perform out‑of‑bounds writes during internal processing. 
An attacker who can control the output of the diff program used by diff3 (e.g. via --diff-program pointing to a malicious script) can trigger out-of-bounds writes, resulting in a crash and potentially remote code execution depending on the environment.


This issue has been fixed in commit 9ff04d5b84743e331e80b589335a52c5480d1815 

NOTE:
The project maintainers claim that this is not a security issue. They state that the worst outcome this issue can cause is a crash of diff and that it cannot be used to escalate privileges.

Vulnerabilities.Title: A directory traversal bug was discovered when unpacking 3.0 (quilt) so ...
Vulnerabilities.Description: A directory traversal bug was discovered when unpacking 3.0 (quilt) source packages, where the packaging tarball could contain the quilt database directory (.pc) with attacker controlled symlinks, where that in combination with patches that would fail to apply, could be used to make the code used to restore the backup files to either modify or remove the files pointed to by the attacker controlled symlinks.

Vulnerabilities.Title: gcc-toolset-15-gcc: gcc: gcc-toolset-16: gcc: Denial of Service via use-after-free in binary heap erase_if
Vulnerabilities.Description: A flaw was found in GCC. When an application calls the erase_if function on a binary heap priority queue in libstdc++, the library reallocates storage but fails to update its internal entry pointer. An attacker capable of triggering this operation can exploit this use-after-free condition, leading to a Denial of Service (DoS) via an application crash or potential memory corruption.

Vulnerabilities.Title: gcc: Confirmed out-of-bounds read/write in libstdc++ parallel `std
Vulnerabilities.Description: A flaw was found in GCC. An out-of-bounds memory access vulnerability exists in the libstdc++ parallel search implementation due to an undersized internal buffer. A local attacker can exploit this flaw by providing crafted search data to an application compiled with parallel mode, causing the process to crash and leading to a Denial of Service (DoS).

Vulnerabilities.Title: gcc: Integer wrap in `std
Vulnerabilities.Description: A flaw was found in the libstdc++ component of GCC. An attacker who can provide an excessively large element count to a boolean vector (std::vector<bool>) constructor can trigger an integer wrap during internal memory calculations. This issue leaves the container in an inconsistent state, leading to out-of-bounds memory access and resulting in an application crash or a Denial of Service (DoS) during subsequent operations.

Vulnerabilities.Title: gcc: Stack overflow in std::bitset on libstdc++
Vulnerabilities.Description: A flaw was found in GCC libstdc++. When an application extracts data into a bitset from a wide-character stream, internal stack memory allocation fails to properly account for character size and alignment. An attacker capable of supplying crafted input to an affected application could trigger a stack-based buffer overflow leading denial of service (DoS).

Vulnerabilities.Title: libstdc++: overflow leaves streambuf in inconsistent state on I/O error.
Vulnerabilities.Description: A flaw was found in libstdc++. When a byte-by-byte write operation fails during file stream processing, the library may still append data into the internal memory buffer. An attacker capable of inducing repeated write failures in an affected service can trigger a buffer overflow, potentially resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS) or memory corruption.

Vulnerabilities.Title: gcc: libstdc++ integer overflow in `new` operator
Vulnerabilities.Description: A flaw was found in libstdc++. An integer overflow can occur when processing large inputs to the aligned operator new in the C++ library. This vulnerability could lead to an undersized memory allocation, potentially causing memory corruption or application instability.

Vulnerabilities.Title: gcc: Out-of-bounds read in std::from_chars
Vulnerabilities.Description: A flaw was found in gcc. An attacker could cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by passing a string that is not null-terminated to the std::from_chars() function in the libstdc++ library. This issue triggers an out-of-bounds read beyond the allocated buffer, potentially leading to invalid data parsing or an application crash.

Vulnerabilities.Title: acl: Symlink traversal privilege escalation via libacl functions
Vulnerabilities.Description: acl before version 2.4.0 contains a symlink traversal vulnerability in the libacl pathname-based functions acl_get_file(), acl_set_file(), acl_extended_file(), and acl_delete_def_file() that allows local attackers to escalate privileges by replacing any pathname component with a symbolic link. Attackers who control any component of a pathname processed by a privileged caller can redirect ACL read or write operations to arbitrary files or directories, enabling unauthorized manipulation of access control lists and local privilege escalation.

Vulnerabilities.Title: acl: TOCTOU Symlink Traversal via getfacl/setfacl
Vulnerabilities.Description: acl before version 2.4.0 contains a time-of-check to time-of-use (TOCTOU) race condition vulnerability that allows local attackers to escalate privileges by replacing a pathname component with a symbolic link between an lstat() check and subsequent symlink-following operations such as stat(), chown(), chmod(), acl_get_file(), and acl_set_file(). Attackers who control a pathname component can redirect file access control list operations to arbitrary files when getfacl, setfacl, or chacl is invoked by a privileged process over an attacker-controlled path, resulting in local privilege escalation.

Vulnerabilities.Title: glibc: glibc: Memory corruption via out-of-bounds write in wide scanf functions
Vulnerabilities.Description:

Vulnerabilities.Title: glibc: glibc: Denial of Service via out-of-bounds read in CP949 character conversion

To exploit this, the target iconv function needs to set //IGNORE on the destination of the conversion and the input and encoding needs to be attacker controlled.

Vulnerabilities.Title: glibc: glibc: Arbitrary code execution via directory traversal in LANGUAGE environment variable

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: curl: SSH host verification bypass when using schemeless URLs with SFTP/SCP
Vulnerabilities.Description:
When a user invokes curl using a schemeless URL combined with
`--proto-default` sftp (or scp), a disconnect occurs between the tool layer
and libcurl. The tool layer incorrectly infers the URL scheme, which
erroneously bypasses the initialization of critical SSH security options like
CURLOPT_SSH_HOST_PUBLIC_KEY_SHA256 and CURLOPT_SSH_KNOWNHOSTS. Conversely, the
libcurl runtime successfully honors CURLOPT_DEFAULT_PROTOCOL and establishes
the connection via SFTP/SCP as specified. Because the tool layer skipped the
security configuration, these SSH host verification options are silently
omitted, causing curl to connect to an unverified SSH remote host without
throwing an error.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: libcurl: Unauthorized connection reuse due to a logical error
Vulnerabilities.Description:
libcurl might in some circumstances reuse the wrong connection when asked to
do Negotiate-authenticated ones, even when they are set to use different
"services".

libcurl features a pool of recent connections so that subsequent requests can
reuse an existing connection to avoid overhead.

When reusing a connection a range of criteria must be met. Due to a logical
error in the code, a request that was issued by an application could
wrongfully reuse an existing connection to the same server that was
authenticated using different services.

Vulnerabilities.Title: libcurl: libcurl: Use-after-free vulnerability leading to Denial of Service
Vulnerabilities.Description:
A use-after-free vulnerability exists in libcurl when an application
configures an HTTP/2 stream-dependency tree via `CURLOPT_STREAM_DEPENDS` or
`CURLOPT_STREAM_DEPENDS_E`, subsequently invokes `curl_easy_reset()`, and
finally terminates the handle with `curl_easy_cleanup()`. During this final
cleanup phase, libcurl attempts to access and modify an internal structure
that was already freed during the reset operation.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: curl: Information disclosure via incorrect Digest authentication header reuse
Vulnerabilities.Description:
Successfully using libcurl to do a transfer to a specific HTTP origin
(`hostA`) with **Digest** authentication and then changing the origin to a
different one (`hostB`) for a second transfer, reusing the same handle, makes
libcurl wrongly pass on the `Authorization:` header field meant for `hostA`,
to `hostB`.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: libcurl: Information disclosure via incorrect connection reuse with Negotiate authentication
Vulnerabilities.Description:
A flaw in libcurl makes it wrongly reuse an HTTP connection setup for a given
hostname using Negotiate authentication, when the initial request is done
using empty credentials. This can make user B's request get sent over user A's
previously authenticated connection.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: curl: Information disclosure via incorrect .netrc password lookup
Vulnerabilities.Description:
When asking curl to use a `.netrc` file to find credentials and at the same
time specifying a URL with a username (without a password), like
`https://user@example.com/`, curl could wrongly get and use the password for
*another* user set in the `.netrc` file for that host if such a one exists and
there is no match for the specified user.

Vulnerabilities.Title: libcurl: libcurl: Security feature bypass due to improper mTLS connection reuse
Vulnerabilities.Description:
libcurl would reuse a previously created connection even when some mTLS config
related option had been changed that should have prohibited reuse.

libcurl keeps previously used connections in a connection pool for subsequent
transfers to reuse if one of them matches the setup. However, some TLS
settings related to client certificates were left out from the configuration
match checks, making them match too easily. In particular options related to
the private key.

Vulnerabilities.Title: libcurl: libcurl: Information disclosure due to failure to clear proxy authentication credentials
Vulnerabilities.Description:
libcurl had a flaw that when instructed to clear proxy authentication
credentials which made it not do so, leaving the old credentials around to get
used for subsequent transfers that should not know nor use them.

Vulnerabilities.Title: libcurl: libcurl: Use-after-free via curl_easy_pause() in CURLMOPT_SOCKETFUNCTION callback
Vulnerabilities.Description:
Calling `curl_easy_pause()` within the event-based `CURLMOPT_SOCKETFUNCTION`
callback triggers a use-after-free vulnerability, where libcurl attempts to
store a flag using a dangling struct pointer immediately after that pointer's
memory has been freed.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: curl: FTP wildcard write callback mixup
Vulnerabilities.Description:
When an FTP wildcard `LIST` operation fails, libcurl omits the restoration
path meant for successful listings, leaving the write callback set to the
internal listing parser and the write callback data pointing directly to the
easy handle. Subsequent reuse of this handle triggers an immediate crash, and
cloning it via `curl_easy_duphandle()` copies this corrupted state into the
duplicate. If the original handle is subsequently freed, executing a transfer
on the cloned handle causes a heap use-after-free read against the dangling
handle reference; alternatively, reusing the original or cloned handle while
changing only  `CURLOPT_WRITEDATA` (and omitting `CURLOPT_WRITEFUNCTION`)
results in type confusion, forcing the internal parser to interpret incoming
server response bytes into memory at the application-supplied write data
pointer.

Vulnerabilities.Title: libcurl: libcurl: Information disclosure via cached SSL session and early data
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In this scenario, libcurl first uses a proper HTTP/3 server for the initial
transfers, and when it makes a second transfer to the same site it has been
replaced by the attacker's impostor machine - without a valid certificate.

When libcurl returns to the hostname the second time with a cached SSL session
(`CURLOPT_SSL_SESSIONID_CACHE` is not disabled) and early data enabled (the
`CURLSSLOPT_EARLYDATA` bit is set in `CURLOPT_SSL_OPTIONS`), libcurl might
send off the second request's bytes on that new connection *before* enforcing
the certificate verification failure. Potentially leaking sensitive
information.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: Curl missing SFTP host verification with wolfSSH backend
Vulnerabilities.Description:
curl's code for managing SSH connections when SFTP was done using the wolfSSH
powered backend was flawed and missed host verification mechanisms.

This prevents curl from detecting MITM attackers and more.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: curl: Security bypass due to global TLS option changes in multi-threaded LDAPS transfers
Vulnerabilities.Description:
When doing multi-threaded LDAPS transfers (LDAP over TLS) with libcurl,
changing TLS options in one thread would inadvertently change them globally
and therefore possibly also affect other concurrently setup transfers.

Disabling certificate verification for a specific transfer could
unintentionally disable the feature for other threads as well.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: Host verification bypass during SSH transfers
Vulnerabilities.Description:
When doing SSH-based transfers using either SCP or SFTP, and setting the
known_hosts file, libcurl could still mistakenly accept connecting to hosts
*not present* in the specified file if they were added as recognized in the
libssh *global* known_hosts file.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: libssh key passphrase bypass without agent set
Vulnerabilities.Description:
When doing SSH-based transfers using either SCP or SFTP, and asked to do
public key authentication, curl would wrongly still ask and authenticate using
a locally running SSH agent.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: curl: info leak uploading over WebSockets with GnuTLS
Vulnerabilities.Description:
When curl is built with GnuTLS, a malicious WebSocket server can make curl
send memory past its send buffer. This is due to an out of bounds read
following when `gnutls_record_send()` returns a number of bytes sent **greater
than the number of bytes it was given to send**. GnuTLS does that after a
blocked send.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: curl: local interface connection reuse mixup
Vulnerabilities.Description:
When `CURLOPT_INTERFACE` (or the command line tool's `--interface` option) is
set with one of the documented prefixes (`if!`, `host!`, `ifhost!`), that
binding is not part of the connection reuse key, so a later transfer asking
for a different source can silently reuse an existing connection and go out
from the earlier transfer's source address

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: curl: Authentication bypass in OpenLDAP SASL negotiation via Man-in-the-Middle (MITM) attack
Vulnerabilities.Description:
A flaw in the libcurl SASL negotiation for LDAP authentication allows an
incomplete handshake sequence to be misinterpreted as a successful
cryptographic verification. An attacker executing a Man-in-the-Middle (MITM)
attack can inject a premature or shortcut response that bypasses complete peer
validation.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: libcurl: Use-after-free in HTTP/2 Server Push with shared connections
Vulnerabilities.Description:
A flaw in libcurl's handling of HTTP/2 Server Push streams, when the parent
handle is set to share connections with other handles, can lead to
use-after-free in the cleanup process.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: libcurl: Memory corruption vulnerability via OpenSSL 3 provider use-after-free
Vulnerabilities.Description:
When performing transfers via libcurl’s multi interface, pooled TLS
connections can outlive their originating easy handles. In OpenSSL 3 provider
configurations, libcurl attaches an allocated library context to the easy
handle's state and passes it to OpenSSL without acquiring an ownership
reference; destroying the easy handle prematurely frees this context while the
active connection retains a dangling pointer, leading to a heap-use-after-free
upon subsequent I/O or post-handshake operations.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: curl: Public key pinning bypass allows unauthenticated connections
Vulnerabilities.Description:
When `CURLOPT_PINNEDPUBLICKEY` is configured alongside options that disable
standard peer verification (`CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYPEER = 0` and
`CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYHOST = 0`), libcurl fails to enforce public key pinning on
connections established without a presented server certificate. Bypassing the
pinning check under these disabled-verification conditions allows
unauthenticated connections to succeed when they should be rejected.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: curl: Information disclosure due to secure cookie attribute bypass
Vulnerabilities.Description:
A `Set-Cookie:` header using tab (horizontal tab, ASCII code 9) instead of
space (ascii code 32) immediately before the `Secure` attribute causes curl to
store the cookie without its Secure flag. The cookie might then wrongfully be
sent over plaintext HTTP on subsequent requests to the same host.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: libcurl: Improper certificate validation when using wolfSSL CA cache
Vulnerabilities.Description:
With the wolfSSL backend, when CA caching is enabled and an
`CURLOPT_SSL_CTX_FUNCTION` callback replaces the trust store, libcurl can
silently reinstall the cached store after the callback returns. A certificate
trusted by the cached store but rejected by the callback-selected store is
then incorrectly accepted.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: libcurl: Information disclosure via improper Public Suffix List boundary check
Vulnerabilities.Description:
When libpsl support is enabled, libcurl fails to enforce the Public Suffix
List boundary check when processing a `Set-Cookie` header where the `Domain`
attribute explicitly matches an origin host that is itself a public suffix
(e.g., `Domain=co.uk` set by `co.uk`).

Instead of coercing it into a strict host-only cookie, libcurl saves the
cookie with wildcard domain scope (`.co.uk`). Consequently, the cookie is
inappropriately included in subsequent outbound requests or HTTP redirects to
arbitrary sibling subdomains under the same public suffix (e.g.,
`attacker.co.uk`).

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: curl: stale SigV4 headers sent unintended
Vulnerabilities.Description:
Setting `CURLOPT_AWS_SIGV4` to NULL but does not disable SigV4 authentication,
contrary to expectations and documentation. A subsequent transfer on the same
handle still sends an `Authorization: AWS4-HMAC-SHA256` header to whatever URL
isset next, leaking state information.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: curl: redirect to SFTP or SCP bypasses host verification
Vulnerabilities.Description:
A flaw in the curl command line tool's logic makes it only set SSH host
verification options when interacting directly using SFTP or SCP, and not as a
result of following a redirect.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: curl: leaking host credentials to HTTP proxy
Vulnerabilities.Description:
An HTTP proxy can trick libcurl into sending the origin's credentials (Basic
password, or a Negotiate/Kerberos ticket) to the proxy itself, by answering
the `CONNECT` tunnel request with 401 `WWW-Authenticate:` instead of the
expected 407 `Proxy-Authenticate:`.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: curl: HSTS cache import drops longer-lived child
Vulnerabilities.Description:
Importing a `includeSubDomains` parent HSTS entry before a longer-lived child
entry, silently drops the child. Consequently, when the parent expires, the
child's valid HSTS policy is lost, causing curl to issue unencrypted HTTP
requests rather than upgrading to HTTPS.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: curl: Hsts Response Erases Persisted Entries
Vulnerabilities.Description:
An authenticated HTTPS origin can supply an HSTS `max-age` value that the
parser accepts, but time serialization later fails to process. On 64-bit
systems, extreme max-age values compute an absolute expiry within standard
time integer limits that exceeds calendar time structure bounds. During cache
saves, the original HSTS file is truncated before writing a temporary
replacement; when serialization fails, the temporary file is deleted, leaving
an empty or partial cache. Because the save error is silently ignored during
cleanup, curl exits successfully despite the data loss.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: IMAP APPEND plus CRLF conversion command injection
Vulnerabilities.Description:
Enabling `CURLOPT_CRLF` causes curl to advertise the raw input byte count in
the `IMAP APPEND {N}` literal while transmitting line-ending expanded data.
The server reads only $N$ bytes for the payload, causing the remaining
overflow bytes to be interpreted and executed as pipelined IMAP commands
within the authenticated session.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: curl: knownhost callback mismatches key as missing
Vulnerabilities.Description:
When libcurl uses libssh2 with a hashed `known_hosts` file, an unrelated
initial entry can cause host key validation to report a key *mismatch* as a
*missing* key to the `CURLOPT_SSH_KEYFUNCTION` callback.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: curl: wolfSSL public-key pinning bypass
Vulnerabilities.Description:
When built with wolfSSL, curl can successfully validate a pinned public key
hash against a key the TLS peer does not possess. During the TLS handshake,
wolfSSL validates the connection, but curl's subsequent re-parsing of the same
certificate - tricked by a manipulated validity length field - extracts and
matches a different embedded key, incorrectly authorizing the pinned public
key.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: curl: server-set cookie aborts cookie jar load
Vulnerabilities.Description:
When writing a long cookie name and value to a Netscape cookie jar, a remote
HTTP server can make `curl` write a record that exceeds its line-length
parsing limit. Consequently, any subsequent `curl` invocation reading from
that same cookie jar using `--cookie` silently aborts parsing prematurely upon
encountering the too long line, ignoring all subsequent valid cookies in the
file.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: curl: never-ending loop via server response omission
Vulnerabilities.Description:
By permanently omitting the final control-response line, a malicious FTP,
IMAP, POP3, or SMTP server can exploit libcurl and completely bypass its
configured transfer timeout mechanism, indefinitely blocking all concurrent
transfers bound to the same multi-handle.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: curl: TFTP direction confusion
Vulnerabilities.Description:
libcurl's TFTP state machine fails to validate state transitions against the
requested transfer direction, accepting opening server responses for both
reads and writes interchangeably. A malicious TFTP server can respond to a
download request in a way that forces the client into transmit mode, prompting
libcurl to consume and transmit data from the handle's persistent
`CURLOPT_READDATA` pointer - including data remaining from unrelated prior
operations, such as an HTTP POST request executed on a reused handle.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: curl: -J no-clobber guarantee bypassed with 103 early hints
Vulnerabilities.Description:
When invoked with `--remote-header-name` (`-J`), curl fails to preserve its
documented anti-clobbering protection if an intermediate 103 Early Hints
response precedes the final HTTP response, or if an `ETag` header is processed
before `Content-Disposition` under `--etag-save`. This flaw allows an HTTP(S)
server to overwrite an existing local file specified in the
`Content-Disposition` header despite the presence of the `-J` non-overwrite
constraint.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: curl: curl_mime_free stack overflow by recursion
Vulnerabilities.Description:
A deeply nested multipart MIME structure constructed via the public API causes
a stack overflow in libcurl during normal cleanup operations. An excessive
recursion depth within `curl_mime_free` leads to unbounded stack frame
allocation during structure traversal, ultimately crashing the host process.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: curl: password leak in CURLINFO_EFFECTIVE_URL
Vulnerabilities.Description:
libcurl could accidentally return a URL for `curl_easy_getinfo()`'s
`CURLINFO_EFFECTIVE_URL` option containing credentials, even though neither
the URL provided to libcurl nor the redirected URL did.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: curl: Man-in-the-middle attack via SSH host key bypass
Vulnerabilities.Description:
When a libcurl-based application performs transfers via `SCP://` or `SFTP://`
and utilizes the `CURLOPT_SSH_KEYFUNCTION` callback, it may silently accept an
untrusted server. This vulnerability occurs when a server presents a host key
type that does not match the specific key type already recorded for that host
in the `known_hosts` file. Instead of rejecting the mismatch, the callback
mechanism fails to properly enforce the restriction, allowing the connection
to succeed without warning and risking a potential man-in-the-middle attack.

Vulnerabilities.Title: libde265 commit 4d45a6b contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerabil ...
Vulnerabilities.Description: libde265 commit 4d45a6b contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in the NAL parsing path. When de265_push_NAL() is called with a zero-length NAL unit, the resulting NAL_unit may retain a NULL backing buffer, which is subsequently passed as the destination argument to memcpy() in NAL_unit::set_data(). Although the copy length is zero, this violates the nonnull requirement of memcpy() and results in undefined behavior, causing process termination in UBSan-instrumented builds and denial of service.

Vulnerabilities.Title: [GHSA-mm7m-v26f-wf8x: heap-use-after-free in decoder_context::reset() via dangling previous_slice_header]
[GHSA-xp3h-6f5r-8cxp: Concurrent Execution using Shared Resource with Improper Synchronization ('Race Condition') and Use After Free and Double Free in libde265]
gcc-toolset-15-gcc: gcc: gcc-toolset-16: gcc: Denial of Service via use-after-free in binary heap erase_if
Vulnerabilities.Description: A flaw was found in GCC. When an application calls the erase_if function on a binary heap priority queue in libstdc++, the library reallocates storage but fails to update its internal entry pointer. An attacker capable of triggering this operation can exploit this use-after-free condition, leading to a Denial of Service (DoS) via an application crash or potential memory corruption.

A local attacker can exploit this flaw by providing crafted search data to an application compiled with parallel mode, causing the process to crash and leading to a Denial of Service (DoS).

Vulnerabilities.Title: gcc: Integer wrap in `std
Vulnerabilities.Description: A flaw was found in the libstdc++ component of GCC. An attacker who can provide an excessively large element count to a boolean vector (std::vector<bool>) constructor can trigger an integer wrap during internal memory calculations. This issue leaves the container in an inconsistent state, leading to out-of-bounds memory access and resulting in an application crash or a Denial of Service (DoS) during subsequent operations.

Vulnerabilities.Title: gcc: Stack overflow in std::bitset on libstdc++
Vulnerabilities.Description: A flaw was found in GCC libstdc++. When an application extracts data into a bitset from a wide-character stream, internal stack memory allocation fails to properly account for character size and alignment. An attacker capable of supplying crafted input to an affected application could trigger a stack-based buffer overflow leading denial of service (DoS).

Vulnerabilities.Title: libstdc++: overflow leaves streambuf in inconsistent state on I/O error.
Vulnerabilities.Description: A flaw was found in libstdc++. When a byte-by-byte write operation fails during file stream processing, the library may still append data into the internal memory buffer. An attacker capable of inducing repeated write failures in an affected service can trigger a buffer overflow, potentially resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS) or memory corruption.

Vulnerabilities.Title: gcc: libstdc++ integer overflow in `new` operator
Vulnerabilities.Description: A flaw was found in libstdc++. An integer overflow can occur when processing large inputs to the aligned operator new in the C++ library. This vulnerability could lead to an undersized memory allocation, potentially causing memory corruption or application instability.

Vulnerabilities.Title: gcc: Out-of-bounds read in std::from_chars
Vulnerabilities.Description: A flaw was found in gcc. An attacker could cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by passing a string that is not null-terminated to the std::from_chars() function in the libstdc++ library. This issue triggers an out-of-bounds read beyond the allocated buffer, potentially leading to invalid data parsing or an application crash.

Vulnerabilities.Title: libgcrypt: ElGamal implementation doesn't have semantic security due to incorrectly encoded plaintexts possibly allowing to obtain sensitive information
Vulnerabilities.Description: cipher/elgamal.c in Libgcrypt through 1.8.2, when used to encrypt messages directly, improperly encodes plaintexts, which allows attackers to obtain sensitive information by reading ciphertext data (i.e., it does not have semantic security in face of a ciphertext-only attack). The Decisional Diffie-Hellman (DDH) assumption does not hold for Libgcrypt's ElGamal implementation.

Vulnerabilities.Title: libgcrypt: vulnerable to Marvin Attack
Vulnerabilities.Description: A timing-based side-channel flaw was found in libgcrypt's RSA implementation. This issue may allow a remote attacker to initiate a Bleichenbacher-style attack, which can lead to the decryption of RSA ciphertexts.

Vulnerabilities.Title: HTTPS: block-wise chosen-plaintext attack against SSL/TLS (BEAST)
Vulnerabilities.Description: The SSL protocol, as used in certain configurations in Microsoft Windows and Microsoft Internet Explorer, Mozilla Firefox, Google Chrome, Opera, and other products, encrypts data by using CBC mode with chained initialization vectors, which allows man-in-the-middle attackers to obtain plaintext HTTP headers via a blockwise chosen-boundary attack (BCBA) on an HTTPS session, in conjunction with JavaScript code that uses (1) the HTML5 WebSocket API, (2) the Java URLConnection API, or (3) the Silverlight WebClient API, aka a "BEAST" attack.

Vulnerabilities.Title: gnutls: gnutls: Information disclosure via contradictory Key Usage and Extended Key Usage extensions
Vulnerabilities.Description: GnuTLS v3.8.13 does not reject end-entity X.509 certificates that contain a contradictory combination of Key Usage (KU) and Extended Key Usage (EKU). NOTE: the Supplier does not consider this an actionable security vulnerability because of its "threat model doesn't consider attacks only possible by modifying anything within the trust boundary (private keys, trusted certificate authorities and their issued certificates including intermediate CAs, etc.)" policy.

Vulnerabilities.Title: gnutls: gnutls: legitimate user certificates incorrectly rejected causing denial of service

NOTE: the Supplier does not consider this an actionable security vulnerability because of its "threat model doesn't consider attacks only possible by modifying anything within the trust boundary (private keys, trusted certificate authorities and their issued certificates including intermediate CAs, etc.)" policy.

Vulnerabilities.Title: gnutls: gnutls: certificates with invalid extensions incorrectly accepted
Vulnerabilities.Description: GnuTLS v3.8.13 does not reject a critical keyUsage extension when it cannot be processed, such as when extnValue is an ASN.1 NULL (05 00) instead of a BIT STRING. NOTE: the Supplier does not consider this an actionable security vulnerability because of its "threat model doesn't consider attacks only possible by modifying anything within the trust boundary (private keys, trusted certificate authorities and their issued certificates including intermediate CAs, etc.)" policy.

Vulnerabilities.Description: The certificate authentication info handling in gnutls from 2.5.9 up to 3.8.13 does not reset the certificate count and list pointer when re-allocation of raw_certificate_list fails, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service for a peer under heap pressure.

Vulnerabilities.Title: The RSA-PSK ClientKeyExchange handler in gnutls before 3.8.14 does not ...
Vulnerabilities.Description: The RSA-PSK ClientKeyExchange handler in gnutls before 3.8.14 does not return after detecting a memory allocation failure when copying the PSK username, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service for a peer under heap pressure.

Vulnerabilities.Title: A double free in the X.509 name constraints enforcement of GnuTLS 3.8. ...
Vulnerabilities.Description: A double free in the X.509 name constraints enforcement of GnuTLS 3.8.13 on all platforms allows a remote attacker to cause a denial of service (application crash) via a certificate chain containing a NameConstraints extension processed while the application is under memory pressure. When an already populated name constraints object is reinitialized, previously freed list pointers are not cleared, so a memory allocation failure precisely at reinitialization leaves a dangling pointer that is freed again during a later cleanup.

Vulnerabilities.Description: An issue was discovered in MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) through 1.16. There is a variable "dbentry->n_key_data" in kadmin/dbutil/dump.c that can store 16-bit data but unknowingly the developer has assigned a "u4" variable to it, which is for 32-bit data. An attacker can use this vulnerability to affect other artifacts of the database as we know that a Kerberos database dump file contains trusted data.

Vulnerabilities.Title: sqlite: sqlite: Denial of Service via stack exhaustion in countOfViewOptimization()
Vulnerabilities.Description: SQLite before 3.54.0 contains a stack exhaustion vulnerability in countOfViewOptimization() that allows attackers to crash the host process via count(*) over a large multi-row VALUES clause. Attackers supplying SQL or a database file with a crafted view can trigger deeply nested TK_PLUS expressions whose recursive freeing in sqlite3ExprDeleteNN() exhausts the C stack, causing denial of service.

Vulnerabilities.Title: sqlite: SQLite: Denial of Service via malformed changeset in Session Extension
Vulnerabilities.Description: A NULL pointer dereference in the SQLite Session Extension in SQLite 3.53.1 and SQLite trunk builds before check-in e807d4e3798efd53 allows an attacker who can supply a malformed changeset blob to cause a denial of service. The issue occurs when sqlite3changeset_apply_v3() applies a corrupt changeset and reaches sqlite3_value_type() with a NULL sqlite3_value pointer.

Vulnerabilities.Title: sqlite: SQLite: Information disclosure via Session Extension changeset merge path
Vulnerabilities.Description: An issue in SQLite before Fossil check-in 869a51ae84df allows a local attacker to obtain sensitive information via the Session Extension changeset concat/changegroup merge path

Vulnerabilities.Title: sqlite: crafted SQL query allows a malicious user to obtain sensitive information
Vulnerabilities.Description: A Memory Leak vulnerability exists in SQLite Project SQLite3 3.35.1 and 3.37.0 via maliciously crafted SQL Queries (made via editing the Database File), it is possible to query a record, and leak subsequent bytes of memory that extend beyond the record, which could let a malicious user obtain sensitive information. NOTE: The developer disputes this as a vulnerability stating that If you give SQLite a corrupted database file and submit a query against the database, it might read parts of the database that you did not intend or expect.

Vulnerabilities.Title: sqlite: SQLite: Information Disclosure via Crafted ZIP File
Vulnerabilities.Description: An information disclosure issue in the zipfileInflate function in the zipfile extension in SQLite v3.51.1 and earlier allows attackers to obtain heap memory via supplying a crafted ZIP file.

Vulnerabilities.Title: sqlite: sqlite: Authorization bypass via USING clause in JOIN queries
Vulnerabilities.Description: SQLite before 3.54.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in lookupName() that invokes the authorizer only for the first joined table's USING column. Attackers able to submit SQL can query a shared USING column in a RIGHT or FULL JOIN to read columns denied via sqlite3_set_authorizer() SQLITE_READ restrictions.

Vulnerabilities.Title: openssl: OpenSSL: Denial of Service via unbounded QUIC frame queueing
Vulnerabilities.Description:
Issue summary: The QUIC stack queues a RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frame also for
retransmitted NEW_CONNECTION_ID frames. This allows a remote malicious
QUIC stack to queue an unlimited number of RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frames.

Impact summary: A malicious remote QUIC peer can trigger an out-of-memory
condition causing a Denial of Service.

CWE: CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

Description: The earlier fix for CVE-2026-84784 was not complete. It
failed to ignore retransmissions of the NEW_CONNECTION_ID frame. The QUIC
implementation created and inserted a RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frame for every
retransmitted NEW_CONNECTION_ID frame it received and there was no limit
on how many RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frames were queued.

This issue allows a malicious remote QUIC stack to trigger an unbounded
allocation of memory and eventually an out-of-memory (OOM) condition.

FIPS impact: no
The FIPS module is not affected as the QUIC implementation is outside the
OpenSSL FIPS module boundary.

Vulnerabilities.Title: openssl: openssl: Denial of Service via memory leak in QUIC stream handling
Vulnerabilities.Description:
Issue summary: A QUIC server that rejects a stream opened by the peer may
retain that stream's state for the lifetime of the connection if the peer
resets the stream before the rejection is signalled, even though the peer's
stream credit is returned.

Impact summary: A remote client that completes a QUIC handshake can repeatedly
open and reset streams, causing server memory to grow without bound until the
process runs out of memory and every connection on it is lost. This is a
Denial of Service.

CWE: CWE-401: Missing Release of Memory after Effective Lifetime

Description: QUIC servers track each stream the peer opens. When the incoming
stream policy rejects a stream, OpenSSL schedules a STOP_SENDING frame, marks
the stream deleted and returns the peer's stream credit. A deleted stream is
collected only once its receive part is fully drained, which for a rejected
stream means the STOP_SENDING has been acknowledged. If the peer sends
RESET_STREAM first, the reset cancels the pending STOP_SENDING, so it is never
sent or acknowledged and the stream is never collected.

The default configuration reaches this path. Once a connection has a default
stream, meaning the application has read from or written to the connection as
the tutorial server does, the effective incoming stream policy rejects streams
the application does not accept. Applications that set the REJECT policy
explicitly are affected too.

Each retained stream costs about 300 bytes, and the peer's stream credit
window paces how quickly they accumulate. A client that keeps the connection
open and keeps opening and resetting streams grows server memory without
bound. The severity is Low because growth is slow, needs a long-lived
connection, and causes no memory corruption or disclosure.

FIPS impact: no
The affected code is outside the FIPS module boundary.

Vulnerabilities.Title: openssl: openssl: Denial of Service via crafted EC certificate in CMS encryption
Vulnerabilities.Description:
Issue summary: Encrypting a CMS message to an EC certificate whose group order
is 1 may cause CMS_encrypt() or CMS_encrypt_ex() to loop indefinitely.

Impact summary: An attacker able to supply the recipient certificate to an
application performing CMS encryption can cause that application to loop
indefinitely, consuming CPU and resulting in Denial of Service.

CWE: CWE-835: Loop with Unreachable Exit Condition ('Infinite Loop')

Description: CMS_encrypt() and CMS_encrypt_ex() encrypt a message to one or
more recipient certificates and, for an EC recipient, generate an ephemeral
key in the recipient's group. If the certificate declares a group order of 1,
random scalar generation can only produce zero. The key generation routine
then retries without limit while waiting for a nonzero private scalar, so the
call never returns.

The OpenSSL TLS and QUIC implementations do not use this path. An application
is exposed only if it calls CMS_encrypt() or CMS_encrypt_ex() with a recipient
certificate whose EC parameters are attacker-controlled. Certificates with
normal EC group orders do not trigger the loop.

OpenSSL 4.0 and later reject unknown explicit EC groups in default builds.
These versions are affected only when configured with the
enable-ec_explicit_curves option.

The result is a hang that consumes a CPU core until the process is
interrupted, a Denial of Service. The severity is Low because the attacker
must supply the recipient certificate and the application must choose to
encrypt to it; ordinary CMS encryption to trusted recipients is unaffected.

The fix makes EC key generation fail when the group has no valid nonzero
private scalar, instead of retrying indefinitely.

FIPS impact: no
The FIPS modules in 4.1, 4.0, 3.5 and 3.0 are not affected. The FIPS provider
does not support arbitrary explicit EC domain parameters, so an order-1 group
is rejected during key import before the vulnerable key generation path is
reached.

Vulnerabilities.Title: openssl: openssl: Denial of Service via crafted CMS or PKCS#7 SignedData message
Vulnerabilities.Description:
Issue summary: Verifying a maliciously crafted CMS or PKCS#7 SignedData
message with CRL checking enabled may consume excessive CPU time, growing with
the square of the message size.

Impact summary: An attacker who can submit a CMS or PKCS#7 SignedData message
to an application that verifies it with CRL checking enabled can occupy a CPU
core for seconds to minutes, causing Denial of Service. Applications that
leave CRL checking disabled are not affected.

CWE: CWE-407: Inefficient Algorithmic Complexity

Description: With CRL checking enabled, OpenSSL compares each CRL distribution
point of a certificate against the issuing distribution point of every
candidate CRL. For a nameRelativeToCRLIssuer distribution point, the full name
is the CRL issuer name with the relative name appended. Since the change that
deferred this computation, crl_crldp_check() rebuilds that full name for each
candidate CRL and frees it again.

CMS_verify() and PKCS7_verify() take both the distribution points and the
candidate CRLs from the message, and this scoring runs before any signature is
checked. An application is exposed only if it sets X509_V_FLAG_CRL_CHECK on
the store and does not pass CMS_NOCRL or PKCS7_NOCRL; CRL checking is off by
default. In TLS the CRLs come from the local store, so a peer controls only
the distribution point count.

The cost grows with the product of the distribution point count, the CRL count
and the issuer name length, all chosen by the message author; a few hundred
kilobytes can occupy a CPU core for tens of seconds. Verification still fails
as it should, with no crash, no incorrect result and no memory growth.
Requiring CRL checking is what limits the severity.

FIPS impact: no
The affected code is outside the FIPS module boundary.

Vulnerabilities.Title: openssl: openssl: Denial of Service via out-of-bounds read during TLS key-share processing
Vulnerabilities.Description:
Issue summary: A server configured with the Suite B certificate flag through
SSL_CTX_set_cert_flags() and with TLS 1.3 enabled may read past the end of a
fixed group list when it processes a ClientHello whose supported_groups and
key_share contain no Suite B group.

Impact summary: A remote client can send a ClientHello that makes the server
read past the end of a static array. The values read are never returned to the
client, so no memory is disclosed; on builds with sanitizers or hardened
allocators the read may crash the process, causing Denial of Service.

CWE: CWE-125: Out-of-bounds Read

Description: When the Suite B certificate flag is set, OpenSSL restricts the
accepted groups to P-256 and P-384 by substituting a fixed two-element list
for the configured group list. The tuple machinery used for key-share
selection was not updated for this substitution: tls1_get_group_tuples() still
returns the configured tuples, which by default describe eight groups. The
server-side walk in tls_parse_ctos_key_share() then advances through the
two-element list using those tuple counts without checking the cumulative
offset against the number of groups present.

Only applications that call SSL_CTX_set_cert_flags() with
SSL_CERT_FLAG_SUITEB_128_LOS and leave TLS 1.3 enabled are affected. The
openssl s_server -suiteB_128 option sets an X.509 verification parameter
instead, so the stock command line server is not vulnerable. Default
configurations do not reach this code.

A client that offers only groups outside the Suite B set, such as X25519,
forces every tuple to be walked and the read to run past the array. The bytes
read are compared against client group IDs and never sent back, so no memory
is disclosed. On builds with address sanitizers or hardened allocators the
read can abort the process; in ordinary release builds it reads a few bytes of
adjacent constant data.

FIPS impact: no
The affected code is outside the FIPS module boundary.

Vulnerabilities.Title: openssl: OpenSSL: Denial of Service via NULL pointer dereference during DANE TLSA record processing
Vulnerabilities.Description:
Issue summary: A DANE-enabled TLS client may crash by dereferencing a NULL
pointer when processing an unusual combination of certificate and TLSA
records.

Impact summary: The impact is limited to a client crash (potential Denial
of Service).

CWE: CWE-476: NULL Pointer Dereference

Description: A DANE-enabled TLS client that supports TLSA records with at
least one of the PKIX-TA(0) or PKIX-EE(1) usages alongside the DANE-TA(2)
usage may crash by dereferencing a NULL pointer if the server claims a trusted
CA's certificate to be its end-entity certificate and has an unusual mix of
associated TLSA records.

DANE SMTP clients should not be affected since only the
DANE-TA(2) and DANE-EE(3) TLSA record usages are specified applicable
in SMTP.  For example, the Postfix MTA is not affected, while the Exim
MTA does not at present use OpenSSL's DANE implementation.

Use of DANE in validation of RFC7250 raw public keys (RPKs) is also
unaffected, as these only use DANE-EE(3) TLSA records.

Only applications that support combining the DANE PKI with a traditional PKI
are potentially affected.  A DANE-enabled browser or similar, that uses
OpenSSL's DANE API could be affected.

FIPS impact: no
The DANE API is outside the FIPS module boundary.

Vulnerabilities.Title: openssl: openssl: Denial of service via crafted out-of-sequence DTLS handshake fragments
Vulnerabilities.Description:
Issue summary: Receiving crafted out-of-sequence DTLS handshake fragments may
cause OpenSSL to allocate a full message-length reassembly buffer for each
buffered message, so a small amount of wire data consumes a large amount of
memory.

Impact summary: A remote attacker can send a few small crafted DTLS handshake
fragments to make a DTLS server or client allocate well over a megabyte of
memory per connection, which may lead to memory exhaustion and Denial of
Service if many connections are made.

CWE: CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

Description: DTLS handshake messages can arrive out of order and fragmented,
so OpenSSL buffers fragments of up to ten out-of-sequence messages until
reassembly is possible. When the first fragment of a new message arrives,
OpenSSL allocates a buffer sized to the full message length declared in the
fragment header, plus a reassembly bitmap, instead of storing only the bytes
actually received. The declared length is capped by the maximum certificate
list size, 128KB by default, and that cap applies to every handshake message
type rather than only to Certificate messages.

Only DTLS endpoints reach this code. TLS, QUIC and applications that do not
use DTLS are unaffected. An attacker sends fragments that declare a large
message length but carry almost no data, using up to ten distinct message
sequence numbers.

A single connection can then hold roughly 1.4MB of buffers from about 156
bytes on the wire. Because the number of buffered messages is capped, memory
exhaustion requires many connections or many peers, which is why the severity
is Low.

FIPS impact: no
The affected code is outside the FIPS module boundary.

Vulnerabilities.Title: openssl: openssl: Denial of Service via overlapping QUIC CRYPTO frame processing
Vulnerabilities.Description:
Issue summary: A retransmitted QUIC CRYPTO frame can release packet storage
while the TLS record layer retains a direct pointer into that storage causing
use after free.

Impact summary: A malicious QUIC server can cause a heap-use-after-free read
in the OpenSSL QUIC client. The server can also identify one allocator-adjacent
byte through the client's protected Handshake response.

CWE: CWE-416: Use After Free

Description: During CRYPTO stream processing, a pointer into the first frame's
memory on the stream is lent to the TLS handshake processing. The memory
must remain stable until it is processed and released. However the processing
of retransmitted CRYPTO frames could release the memory if the retransmitted
frame fully overlapped the existing frame. This then causes use-after-free read
when the TLS handshake processing continues.

The use-after-free read can lead to a Denial-of-Service of the client
application or a minor leak of information about the heap memory contents
that might be overwritten with other data, subsequently allocated by
the application, to the peer.

FIPS impact: no
The FIPS module is not affected as the QUIC implementation is outside of
the OpenSSL FIPS module boundary.

Vulnerabilities.Title: openssl: OpenSSL: Denial of Service via out-of-bounds read in AES-GCM-SIV
Vulnerabilities.Description:
Issue summary: Setting an AES-GCM-SIV IV shorter than the expected nonce
length via EVP_CipherInit_ex() may trigger a heap out-of-bounds read.
Supplying a longer IV is silently truncated instead of rejected.

Impact summary: An application passing a caller-supplied IV of the wrong
length may crash or read beyond its buffer. Because trailing IV bytes are
ignored, an attacker who knows one message and tag may forge messages under a
different IV.

CWE: CWE-125: Out-of-bounds Read

Description: AES-GCM-SIV copies the caller-supplied IV or nonce into its
internal state using a copy whose length is taken from the expected nonce size
rather than from the length the caller actually provided. When the caller
passes a shorter IV, the copy reads past the end of the caller's buffer;
AddressSanitizer confirms a heap out-of-bounds read reached through
EVP_CipherInit_ex() into ossl_aes_gcm_siv_init(). When the caller passes a
longer IV, the implementation silently discards the trailing bytes instead of
rejecting the length.

The truncation breaks the binding between the IV and the computed
authentication tag. An attacker who has observed a message and its tag under
one IV can produce a message and tag that verify under a different IV whose
first bytes match, since the surplus bytes never influence the computation.
The message itself is unchanged, so this is a failure of IV commitment rather
than a classic existential forgery.

Only applications that call EVP_CipherInit_ex() (or the equivalent provider
cipher initialization) with an IV length other than the standard 12 bytes for
AES-GCM-SIV are affected. The severity is limited because the out-of-bounds
read is small and attacker-controlled only in length, and the forgery requires
an unusual IV length choice by the application.

FIPS impact: no
The FIPS modules are not affected by this issue, as AES-GCM-SIV is not an
approved algorithm.

Vulnerabilities.Title: openssl: openssl: Denial of Service via malformed PEM data in PEM_X509_INFO_read_bio_ex
Vulnerabilities.Description:
Issue summary: When an application passes a stack to
PEM_X509_INFO_read_bio_ex() to add entries to, and reading fails,
OpenSSL frees every entry in the stack, both the old ones and any new
ones, but leaves them in the stack.

Impact summary: An application that passes an existing stack to
PEM_X509_INFO_read_bio_ex() and keeps using it after a failed read may
use memory that was already freed. This can cause a crash or, in
principle, memory corruption. Malformed PEM data can make the read fail,
but only applications that pass an existing stack are affected, and
OpenSSL itself does not do this.

CWE: CWE-416: Use After Free

Description: PEM_X509_INFO_read_bio_ex() reads certificates, CRLs and
private keys from PEM data and adds them to a stack of X509_INFO
structures. If the application passes a stack that is not NULL, the
function adds the new entries to it and must leave the entries that are
already there unchanged.

If reading fails, the function frees every entry in the stack. This
includes the entries that were there before the call, and the entries
added by the call. It does not remove these entries from the stack, so
the stack keeps pointers to freed memory. The failure can happen at any
point, even before any entry was added. A PEM item with invalid content
is enough.  This also happens if the stack was empty: entries added
before the failure are freed but stay in the stack.

An application that then reads or frees the stack will use memory that
was already freed. This can crash the application or, in principle,
corrupt memory.

Only applications that pass a stack that is not NULL are affected.
OpenSSL itself never does this. Its own callers, including the code that
TLS uses to load CA certificates, always pass NULL. When the stack is
NULL, the function frees only the entries that it created itself, which
is safe. We expect that very few applications pass an existing stack. An
attacker can make the read fail with malformed PEM data, but cannot make
an application pass an existing stack.

The same problem affects PEM_X509_INFO_read_bio(), PEM_X509_INFO_read()
and PEM_X509_INFO_read_ex(), which use the same code. OpenSSL 1.1.1 and
1.0.2 have only the first two of these functions.

FIPS impact: no
The affected code is outside the FIPS module boundary.

Vulnerabilities.Title: openssl: openssl: Out-of-bounds write via integer overflow in EVP_EncodeBlock()
Vulnerabilities.Description:
Issue summary: Calling EVP_EncodeBlock() with an input length close to INT_MAX
may overflow the calculation of the encoded output size and write past the end
of the caller-supplied output buffer.

Impact summary: No path by which an attacker can trigger this has been
identified. An application that passes an input length near INT_MAX to
EVP_EncodeBlock() could suffer a heap buffer overflow, crashing or corrupting
its own memory, but it must itself supply such a length.

CWE: CWE-190: Integer Overflow or Wraparound

Description: EVP_EncodeBlock() base64-encodes a buffer of a caller-supplied
length into an output buffer that the caller allocates. The caller is expected
to reserve 4*((len+2)/3)+1 bytes. For input lengths close to INT_MAX, the
arithmetic that computes the encoded length overflows a signed integer, so the
function writes more data than the documented output size. The result is a
heap buffer overflow in the calling process.

Reaching this requires an application to pass an input length near INT_MAX to
EVP_EncodeBlock(). OpenSSL's TLS, QUIC and CMS implementations never encode
buffers of that size, and the command line tools cannot practically be made to
do so: the limits on reading a proxy password from a file and on bignum sizes
prevent it. An application that accepts an attacker-controlled length and
forwards it to EVP_EncodeBlock() without its own bound check is exposed.

The severity is Low because no attacker-controlled path to the overflow is
known. The caller must already hold a buffer of about two gigabytes before the
defect can be reached.

FIPS impact: no
The affected code is outside the FIPS module boundary.

Vulnerabilities.Title: openssl: openssl: Information disclosure via uninitialized memory in QUIC peer detection
Vulnerabilities.Description:
Issue summary: QUIC, when performing automated peer detection, may allow
uninitialized stack data to leak into the received address which is then used
as the destination for outgoing packets.

Impact summary: Applications using QUIC's automated peer detection mechanism
may receive an invalid address, leading to connection loss and disclosure of
uninitialized stack data to an attacker observing the outgoing network traffic.

CWE: CWE-457 (Use of Uninitialized Variable)

Description: The OpenSSL QUIC stack contains a feature in which, when using an
already connected socket, it will auto-detect the peer address during the SSL
handshake.  This feature uses the getpeername() function, passing a buffer of
sufficient length to hold any supported address family, but passes a buffer
length that is only sized such that larger addresses, such as IPv6, cannot be
retrieved. The getpeername() function however, still returns the full address
length, which is accepted as the valid input buffer length, leading to the
address buffer containing uninitialized stack data instead of the actual peer
address. The invalid peer address is then used as destination for the outgoing
packets which leads to a connectivity breakage and a leakage of the
uninitialized stack data to passive network observers.

FIPS impact: no
The FIPS modules in 4.0, 3.6, 3.5, 3.4, and 3.0 are not affected by this CVE as
the affected protocol is not implemented in the FIPS module.

Vulnerabilities.Title: openssl: OpenSSL: Message authentication bypass via zero-length AAD update
Vulnerabilities.Description:
Issue summary: The AES-GCM-SIV implementation treats a zero-length Additional
Authenticated Data (AAD) update as a reset of all the AAD supplied so far,
instead of leaving the AAD unchanged. An application that supplies its AAD in
several fragments, one of which is empty, therefore produces or verifies
messages whose authentication tag does not cover the AAD supplied before
the empty fragment.

Impact summary: Data an application intended to authenticate alongside a
message is silently left unauthenticated. An attacker can forge the AAD of such
a message.

CWE: CWE-325: Missing Cryptographic Step

Description: An application passing AAD in multiple chunks of which some have
zero length will have the previous AAD chunks effectively unauthenticated. Also,
on context re-initialisation, the AAD was not reset, which meant that any AAD
accumulated from the previous context usage were also included in the AAD of the
new message.

The fix makes a zero-length AAD update a no-op and clears any accumulated AAD
whenever the context is re-initialised with a key or a nonce.
A re-initialisation that only changes parameters keeps the AAD.

FIPS impact: no
The FIPS modules are not affected, as AES-GCM-SIV is not a FIPS approved
algorithm and is implemented only in the default provider, outside the
OpenSSL FIPS module boundary.

Vulnerabilities.Title: [Unbounded Out-of-Order Fragment Reassembly in QUIC Streams]
Vulnerabilities.Description:
Issue summary: A QUIC peer that sends many small out-of-order STREAM fragments
while withholding the first byte of the stream may cause OpenSSL to buffer
a large number of reassembly nodes occupying much larger memory than
the actual data sent.

Impact summary: A remote peer can pin large amounts of memory on a server that
accepts incoming QUIC streams, potentially exhausting memory and causing
Denial of Service.

CWE: CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

Description: QUIC receive flow control limits the highest byte offset a peer
may reach on a stream. It does not limit how many out-of-order fragments the
receiver buffers. OpenSSL allocates a reassembly node for each non-adjacent
STREAM fragment and never caps the count. A peer that opens a stream and sends
many one-byte fragments at increasing offsets, while withholding the first
byte, makes the receiver retain one node per fragment without delivering any
data.

Only applications that accept incoming streams are exposed. With the default
policy, which rejects peer-initiated streams, the stream is torn down before
state accumulates. Because the read side never advances past the missing
prefix, the flow control window never slides and the nodes stay pinned for the
life of the connection.

The per-stream window bounds the highest offset, so the memory one stream can
pin is finite, but it can reach tens of megabytes and, across many streams and
connections, drive memory pressure and Denial of Service. The severity is
limited because the exhaustion is bounded by flow control and requires a
non-default configuration.

FIPS impact: no
The affected code is outside the FIPS module boundary.

Vulnerabilities.Title: gcc-toolset-15-gcc: gcc: gcc-toolset-16: gcc: Denial of Service via use-after-free in binary heap erase_if
Vulnerabilities.Description: A flaw was found in GCC. When an application calls the erase_if function on a binary heap priority queue in libstdc++, the library reallocates storage but fails to update its internal entry pointer. An attacker capable of triggering this operation can exploit this use-after-free condition, leading to a Denial of Service (DoS) via an application crash or potential memory corruption.

Vulnerabilities.Title: gcc: Confirmed out-of-bounds read/write in libstdc++ parallel `std
Vulnerabilities.Description: A flaw was found in GCC. An out-of-bounds memory access vulnerability exists in the libstdc++ parallel search implementation due to an undersized internal buffer. A local attacker can exploit this flaw by providing crafted search data to an application compiled with parallel mode, causing the process to crash and leading to a Denial of Service (DoS).

Vulnerabilities.Title: gcc: Integer wrap in `std
Vulnerabilities.Description: A flaw was found in the libstdc++ component of GCC. An attacker who can provide an excessively large element count to a boolean vector (std::vector<bool>) constructor can trigger an integer wrap during internal memory calculations. This issue leaves the container in an inconsistent state, leading to out-of-bounds memory access and resulting in an application crash or a Denial of Service (DoS) during subsequent operations.

Vulnerabilities.Title: gcc: Stack overflow in std::bitset on libstdc++
Vulnerabilities.Description: A flaw was found in GCC libstdc++. When an application extracts data into a bitset from a wide-character stream, internal stack memory allocation fails to properly account for character size and alignment. An attacker capable of supplying crafted input to an affected application could trigger a stack-based buffer overflow leading denial of service (DoS).

Vulnerabilities.Title: libstdc++: overflow leaves streambuf in inconsistent state on I/O error.
Vulnerabilities.Description: A flaw was found in libstdc++. When a byte-by-byte write operation fails during file stream processing, the library may still append data into the internal memory buffer. An attacker capable of inducing repeated write failures in an affected service can trigger a buffer overflow, potentially resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS) or memory corruption.

Vulnerabilities.Title: gcc: libstdc++ integer overflow in `new` operator
Vulnerabilities.Description: A flaw was found in libstdc++. An integer overflow can occur when processing large inputs to the aligned operator new in the C++ library. This vulnerability could lead to an undersized memory allocation, potentially causing memory corruption or application instability.

Vulnerabilities.Title: gcc: Out-of-bounds read in std::from_chars
Vulnerabilities.Description: A flaw was found in gcc. An attacker could cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by passing a string that is not null-terminated to the std::from_chars() function in the libstdc++ library. This issue triggers an out-of-bounds read beyond the allocated buffer, potentially leading to invalid data parsing or an application crash.

Vulnerabilities.Title: systemd: systemd-homed: Local privilege escalation via missing home-record signature verification
Vulnerabilities.Description: systemd-homed contains a local privilege escalation bug via arbitrary system group addition to a local, logged in, homed-managed user

Vulnerabilities.Title: systemd: systemd-oomd: Unprivileged users can terminate arbitrary processes via IPC API
Vulnerabilities.Description: Local unprivileged users can terminate arbitrary local processes via a systemd-oomd IPC API due to a missing path traversal validation.

Vulnerabilities.Title: systemd: TOCTOU race condition when updating file permissions and SELinux security contexts
Vulnerabilities.Description: systemd, when updating file permissions, allows local users to change the permissions and SELinux security contexts for arbitrary files via a symlink attack on unspecified files.

Vulnerabilities.Description: An issue was discovered in systemd 253. An attacker can modify a sealed log file such that, in some views, not all existing and sealed log messages are displayed. NOTE: the vendor reportedly sent "a reply denying that any of the finding was a security vulnerability."

Vulnerabilities.Title: An issue was discovered in systemd 253. An attacker can truncate a sea ...
Vulnerabilities.Description: An issue was discovered in systemd 253. An attacker can truncate a sealed log file and then resume log sealing such that checking the integrity shows no error, despite modifications.
